points.description: Sets up a correct strategy: reduces to a statement proved by induction on n (or telescoping) with a stronger/localized form, e.g. sum 1/b_k ≥ 1/2 − 1/2^{n+1} via a localization inequality involving products/ordering of the a_k; the induction direction must be workable.

levels.says: Mentions induction or telescoping but with no usable stated claim or with a direction that does not work.

points.description: States and proves the key lemma/localization inequality (e.g. for x=a_k^{2^k} type terms: 1/(1+x^2)-type bound such as 1/(2^k(1+a^{2^k})) + ... ≥ appropriate bound, equivalent to 1/(1+x)+1/(1+y) ≥ 1/(1+sqrt(xy)) when xy ≤ something, or the reference Lemma). The proof must be valid, including the condition on the variables under which it holds.

levels.says: Correct lemma stated but proof incomplete or conditions not verified.
Some localization inequality found but not shown to apply or is only partly correct.

points.description: Uses the ordering a_1≤…≤a_n and product 1 to justify applying the lemma (e.g. a_1 ≤ 1 ≤ a_n, or merging terms into a new sequence that is still ordered with product 1 so the induction hypothesis applies).

levels.says: Uses the ordering/product condition but with a gap or without checking the new sequence is again ordered with product 1.

points.description: Completes the induction: base case (n=2 or n=1 appropriately, with check of the bound 1/2−1/2^{n+1}) and inductive step giving the exact bound, with the equality/sum of the lower bounds computed correctly.

levels.says: Base case or the inductive step is done but not both, or arithmetic of the final bound is flawed.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a valid complete proof: a localization lemma, justified use of ordering and product 1, and a complete induction. Partial credit for attempting induction in a workable direction or finding a valid localization inequality. Minor computational slips cost only a little; a different valid proof earns full marks.
